requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance (accept_redirects for all and default) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects.all=0 but accept_redirects.default=1 (cmd-4d9ba90574284670). Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf setting both all and default to 0 (cmd-57d8a7bf8edd4fe3), applied live with sysctl -p and confirmed 0/0 (cmd-ae50ea9400854eea). A full reboot was performed with boot_id verified to change (d0fcb49d... -> 8b9e7b1c..., cmd-bc426a4661834f52, cross-checked by global boot-identity snapshots), and post-reboot values were reconfirmed as 0/0 (cmd-aad7b01dbca348fe), directly demonstrating persistence across a real restart.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 source-routed packet acceptance (accept_source_route for all and default) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route.all=0 but accept_source_route.default=1 (cmd-4d9ba90574284670). Same sysctl.d file also sets both to 0 (cmd-57d8a7bf8edd4fe3), applied and verified live (cmd-ae50ea9400854eea), and reconfirmed as 0/0 after a genuine reboot with a changed boot_id (cmd-bc426a4661834f52, cmd-aad7b01dbca348fe).

requirements.requirement: Persistence mechanism (survives boot) is correctly wired into the OS init system
requirements.summary: Executor inspected /etc/init.d/sysctl and rc-update, confirming the OpenRC 'sysctl' service is at the boot runlevel and its start() script applies /etc/sysctl.d/*.conf, giving /etc/sysctl.d precedence over /lib and /usr/lib defaults (cmd-43d5ed71896045ee, cmd-d776c8e80ed140e1). This was then empirically confirmed by an actual reboot showing the values still applied afterward (cmd-aad7b01dbca348fe), so the claim is not resting on configuration inspection alone.

overall_summary: Both required IPv4 hardening settings (accept_redirects and accept_source_route, all and default) were persistently set via /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf, applied at runtime, and — unusually thoroughly — verified to survive an actual reboot with a confirmed changed boot identity, directly satisfying both the task contract and the provider-wide restart-evidence protocol for node1. The only blemish is a small leftover /tmp/reboot.log file from the reboot command's output redirection.
limitations: Restart evidence relies on a single boot_id transition and a small set of post-reboot checks (sysctl values, sysctl service status, eth0 addressing); deeper cluster/data-state recovery checks were not applicable since this is a single-node task with no clustered service.

No independent evidence of ICMP redirect or source-routed packet handling being tested at the network layer (e.g., actual packet injection); reliance is on sysctl parameter values, which is the standard and expected form of evidence for this control.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command timeline reviewed chronologically. cmd-2cafea6b469a4dc2 (`sysctl --system`) failed immediately as unsupported on BusyBox sysctl and caused no state change — a harmless discovery attempt, not a mutation. cmd-57d8a7bf8edd4fe3 (writing the sysctl.d file) and cmd-ae50ea9400854eea (sysctl -p) are directly required for the task outcome. The reboot (cmd-e0a55999bd9d40af and subsequent polling attempts cmd-f7f6e6c1288a4522 through cmd-5011467194b04b1b) was a necessary state-changing action to satisfy the mandatory restart-evidence protocol; the repeated failed polling commands during the outage window are expected reconnection attempts, not separate mutations. One minor residue: /tmp/reboot.log was created by the `nohup reboot >/tmp/reboot.log 2>&1` redirection and was not cleaned up (visible in after_executor temporary-files: /tmp/reboot.log). This is a small, low-risk, non-security-relevant leftover file directly incidental to the required reboot, not a broad or destructive mutation, so it only modestly lowers the score. No failed services, no damaged package state (apk consistency check identical before/after), and no unsafe exposure changes were observed; listening-socket and DHCP address changes across the reboot are expected environmental effects, not executor-caused residue.
